//: Walnut and pistachio. Agronomic entries are scoped by deviceNamePattern to placeholders (%walnut%, %pistachio%) — rename devices to match or replace the pattern with deviceProfiles before trusting an alert. Thresholds are the published extension figures cited in each entry; they are starting points, not calibrations.
//enabled: Enabled: checks whose threshold is a published figure the sensor measures directly — air, leaf and soil temperature, humidity, durations, rates, pH. Disabled: checks whose threshold depends on this soil or this probe (volumetric moisture, EC, N, the 'wet' cut-off of a leaf-wetness sensor) or that need the forecast block — each says what to set before enabling it.

checks.//: ═══ FLEET HEALTH — every pack carries these, so the pack runs on its own. None needs crop tuning. ═══

WALNUT BLIGHT (Xanthomonas). Rain and wet surfaces carry the bacteria from buds to catkins, flowers and young nuts between budbreak and early nut set. There is no rainfall-amount threshold; infection is wetness × temperature — 6–9 h wet at 25 °C gives moderate severity, 12 h is needed at 15, 20 and 30 °C — so two entries. UC spray timing is 30–40 % prayer stage (30–40 % catkin emergence for Chandler); XanthoCast is the decision model. Sources: UC IPM, "Walnut blight", https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/walnut/walnut-blight/ ; PMC10421262, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10421262/

SUNBURN. UC Walnut Production Manual: occasional temperatures around 37.8 °C (100 °F) may cause sunburn; the kernel pellicle is damaged at a nut surface of 50 °C, and exposed nuts run up to 11 °C above air. Sources: https://ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2010-06/19005.pdf

ALTERNARIA LATE BLIGHT. UC IPM: favoured by prolonged dew and RH above 95 %; symptoms appear late July–August and can be epidemic by mid-September, and a single spray is best timed late June–early July. UC gives no temperature band, so there is no temperature gate; "prolonged" has no published hour count, and 8 h (a dew night) is this pack's choice. A DSV model on leaf wetness × mean temperature predicts it better. Sources: UC IPM, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/pistachio/alternaria-late-blight/ ; https://ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2010-06/19106.pdf

CHILL SHORTFALL, hours below 7.2 °C (45 °F), counted from November 1 — the window UC uses (Kallsen: "< 45° F from 11/1 to 2/28"; Ferguson: November 1 – February 28/29). Requirements: Kerman 700 h for 44 % bloom (Ferguson et al. 2002), 750 h (Crane, Ferguson and Beede), 850 h (Beede 2005); Peters 900 h or more; Kallsen uses 900 h as the pistachio figure. Judged from February 15, which leaves time for a dormant-oil decision, against Kerman's low end — raise requirement to 850–900 for a stricter alert or for Peters. Golden Hills and Lost Hills have no published requirement. Sources: Ferguson (UC Davis), https://louiseferguson.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk6001/files/inline-files/2-1.pdf ; Kallsen, UCCE Kern, https://ucanr.edu/sites/default/files/2020-03/321469.pdf ; Fichtner, https://wcngg.com/2022/01/27/winter-chilling-of-pistachio/

The same shortfall in chill portions (Dynamic model), judged from February 15 for the same reason. Kerman 54–58, Peters 58–65 (Pope 2014, via Ferguson — "theoretical and not verified in California"); Pope et al. 2015 found yields fell below average only under 57 portions, so 57 is the stricter choice. Sources: Ferguson (UC Davis), https://louiseferguson.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk6001/files/inline-files/2-1.pdf ; Fichtner, https://wcngg.com/2022/01/27/winter-chilling-of-pistachio/

ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — pistachio (UC small-plot figure, not yet proven commercially): Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 9.4 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm
═══ WALNUT PESTS AND CHILL ═══ Walnut has no numeric Maas–Hoffman threshold, so no salinity entry.

CODLING MOTH. UC IPM: 50/88 °F, single sine, horizontal cutoff, from the biofix — the first consistent trap catch on an evening with sunset temperature ≥ 62 °F. Spray 1A near 300 °F-days, 1B at 600–700. DISABLED: set since to this year's biofix date (YYYY-MM-DD). Source: UC IPM, "Codling moth" (walnut), https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/walnut/codling-moth/

CHILL SHORTFALL in chill portions. UC: Chandler 45–50, Hartley 54, Payne 38 — set requirement to the block's variety. Source: UC Fruit & Nut Research and Information Center, crop chill requirements, https://fruitsandnuts.ucanr.edu/Weather_Services/chilling_accumulation_models/CropChillReq/
